extracted.intended_audience: GAP users (computational algebraists, mathematicians, and software developers using GAP)
extracted.subtask_short: GAP reference: modules and finite fields
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP operations, attributes and categories related to free left modules, fields, division rings, Galois actions, finite fields, Conway polynomials, and printing/display of finite field elements. Includes constructors, predicates, attributes and algorithmic notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFiniteDimensional
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFiniteDimensional(M) (property) is true if M is a free left module that is finite dimensional over its left acting domain, and false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates computing Dimension(V) and IsFiniteDimensional(V) for a FreeLeftModule over Rationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: UseBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: UseBasis(V, gens) (operation) — the vectors in the list gens are known to form a basis of the free left module V. UseBasis stores information in V that can be derived from this fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects: gens are stored as left module generators if no such generators were bound (useful if V is an algebra); the dimension of V is stored. Example shows V then 'knows its dimension'.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRowModule
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRowModule(V) (property) — a row module is a free left module whose elements are row vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate identifying modules whose elements are row vectors; used to dispatch functions that expect row-vector modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMatrixModule
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMatrixModule(V) (property) — a matrix module is a free left module whose elements are matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate identifying modules whose elements are matrices; used for delegating tasks to matrix-module-specific methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFullRowModule
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFullRowModule(M) (property) — a full row module is a module R^n for a ring R and a nonnegative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More precisely: a free left module over R with row vectors of same length n and dimension equal to n. Several functions delegate tasks to full row modules (examples: Iterator, Enumerator).

rubrics_metrics.name: FullRowModule
rubrics_metrics.description: FullRowModule(R, n) (function) — is the row module R^n for a ring R and a nonnegative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FullRowModule(Integers,5) prints (Integers^5).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFullMatrixModule
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFullMatrixModule(M) (property) — a full matrix module is a module R[m,n] for a ring R and two nonnegative integers m, n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More precisely: a free left module whose elements are m by n matrices with entries in R and whose dimension equals m*n.

rubrics_metrics.name: FullMatrixModule
rubrics_metrics.description: FullMatrixModule(R, m, n) (function) — is the matrix module R^[m,n] for a ring R and nonnegative integers m and n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FullMatrixModule(GaussianIntegers,3,6) yields (GaussianIntegers^[3,6]).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDivisionRing
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDivisionRing(D) (Category) — a division ring in GAP is a nontrivial associative algebra D with a multiplicative inverse for each nonzero element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: in GAP every division ring is a vector space over a division ring (possibly itself). The field of coefficients is stored as LeftActingDomain(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsField
rubrics_metrics.description: IsField(D) (filter) — a field is a commutative division ring (see IsDivisionRing and IsCommutative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: IsField(GaloisField(16)) true; IsField(Rationals) true. Distinguishes commutative division rings from noncommutative ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field (for several generators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field(z, ...) / Field([F,] list) (function) — returns the smallest field K that contains all the elements z,... or the list. If no subfield F is given, K is constructed as a field over itself; with a field F and list, Field constructs the field generated by F and the elements in list as a vector space over F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to construct field closures/field extensions generated by given elements; examples include finite and abelian number fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultField (for several generators)
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultField(z, ...) / DefaultField(list) (function) — returns a field K that contains the given elements; this field need not be the smallest field containing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for cyclotomic elements DefaultField returns the smallest cyclotomic field containing the elements, even if a smaller number field exists. DefaultField may return a larger (convenient) field than Field.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultFieldByGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultFieldByGenerators([z,...]) (operation) — returns the default field containing the elements z,...; this field may be bigger than the smallest field containing these elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility for constructing a left acting domain for field construction when smallest field is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfDivisionRing
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfDivisionRing(D) (attribute) — generators with respect to addition, multiplication, and taking inverses (the identity cannot be omitted ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists a generating set for the division ring under ring operations and inverses.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfField
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfField(F) (attribute) — generators with respect to addition, multiplication, and taking inverses; same as GeneratorsOfDivisionRing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute returning a generating set for a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: DivisionRingByGenerators / FieldByGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: DivisionRingByGenerators([F,] gens) / FieldByGenerators([F,] gens) (operation) — called with a field F and a list gens of scalars, returns the division ring over F generated by gens. Unary version returns the division ring as a vector space over FieldOverItselfByGenerators(gens). FieldByGenerators is a synonym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs division rings/fields from generators; F optional to specify base.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsDivisionRing / AsField
rubrics_metrics.description: AsDivisionRing([F,] C) / AsField([F,] C) (operation) — if collection C can be regarded as a division ring then AsDivisionRing(C) is that division ring viewed as a vector space over its prime field; otherwise fail. If F is a division ring contained in C then return is viewed as vector space over F. AsField is a synonym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to coerce/interpret collections as division rings or fields when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subfield / SubfieldNC
rubrics_metrics.description: Subfield(F, gens) / SubfieldNC(F, gens) (function) — constructs the subfield of F generated by gens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation for producing subfields; NC variant for noncommutative contexts (implied by name).

rubrics_metrics.name: FieldOverItselfByGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: FieldOverItselfByGenerators([z,...]) (operation) — needed when Field/FieldByGenerators is called without an explicit subfield, to construct a left acting domain for such a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary operation used internally to set up left acting domain when none provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimitiveElement
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimitiveElement(D) (attribute) — an element of D that generates D as a division ring together with the left acting domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a generator element for a division ring when one exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimeField
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimeField(D) (attribute) — the prime field of a division ring D is the smallest field which is contained in D. Example: prime field of characteristic zero fields is Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute providing the smallest contained field inside a division ring/field.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimeField
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPrimeField(D) (attribute) — a division ring is a prime field if it is equal to its prime field (see PrimeField).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate indicating the division ring is exactly its prime field.

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeOverPrimeField
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeOverPrimeField(F) (attribute) — the degree of the field F over its prime field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric attribute used in extension-degree computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefiningPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: DefiningPolynomial(F) (attribute) — is the defining polynomial of the field F as a field extension over the left acting domain of F. A root of the defining polynomial can be computed with RootOfDefiningPolynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives minimal/defining polynomial used when field was constructed via polynomial extension; helpful for reconstruction and algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: RootOfDefiningPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: RootOfDefiningPolynomial(F) (attribute) — is a root in the field F of its defining polynomial as a field extension over the left acting domain of F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit element realizing the extension used to define F.

rubrics_metrics.name: FieldExtension
rubrics_metrics.description: FieldExtension(F, poly) (operation) — is the field obtained on adjoining a root of the irreducible polynomial poly to the field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard constructor for simple algebraic field extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: Subfields(F) (operation) — is the set of all subfields of the field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates subfields; used in structural analysis of fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois theory overview (norm/trace/minimal/trace polynomials/conjugates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text explanation: for finite-degree extension L>K, to each α∈L associate K-linear mapping ϕ_α and matrix M_α; norm is det(M_α), trace is trace(M_α), minimal polynomial μ_α and trace polynomial χ_α are minimal and characteristic polynomials of M_α. Conjugates are roots of χ_α in L; in Galois extensions the conjugates coincide with roots of μ_α and norm/trace equal product/sum of conjugates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on dependencies: MinimalPolynomial(F,z) is polynomial over F; Norm(F,z) uses field extension L>K appropriately; default computational methods: MinimalPolynomial via linear systems, TracePolynomial via powers of minimal polynomial, Norm and Trace via characteristic polynomial coefficients, Conjugates uses factorization. For fields in IsFieldControlledByGaloisGroup there are special methods using known Galois groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaloisGroup (of field)
rubrics_metrics.description: GaloisGroup(F) (attribute) — the Galois group of a field F is the group of all field automorphisms of F that fix the subfield K = LeftActingDomain(F) pointwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the extension F>K need not be Galois. Examples given show Size and properties like IsCyclic, IsAbelian for computed groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinimalPolynomial (over a field)
rubrics_metrics.description: MinimalPolynomial(F, z[, ind]) (operation) — returns the minimal polynomial of z over the field F; a generator of the ideal in F[x] of all polynomials vanishing on z (consistent with general MinimalPolynomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show differing minimal polynomials depending on base field; used extensively in extension computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: TracePolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: TracePolynomial(L, K, z[, inum]) (operation) — returns the polynomial that is the product of (X−c) where c runs over the conjugates of z in the extension L over K; sometimes called the characteristic polynomial of z w.r.t. L>K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned as univariate polynomial over K; linked to CharacteristicPolynomial for field-extension elements. Examples show polynomial outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm([L, [K,]] z) (attribute) — returns the norm of the field element z. If two fields L and K given, norm computed w.r.t. L>K; if only L given LeftActingDomain(L) is default for K; if no field given DefaultField(z) used for L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior depends on which fields provided; used frequently in field arithmetic and algebraic number computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace (of field elements and matrices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace([L, [K,]] z) / Trace(mat) (attribute) — returns the trace of field element z w.r.t. extension L>K (defaults analogous to Norm); Trace(mat) returns sum of diagonal entries of a matrix (note: not compatible with Trace for field elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: one-argument Trace(mat) for matrices is not suitable when matrices are regarded as field elements due to differing definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugates
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugates([L, [K,]] z) (attribute) — returns the list of conjugates of field element z. Field arguments determine extension L>K for which conjugates are taken; defaults analogous to Norm/Trace/DefaultField.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result list may contain duplicates if z lies in a proper subfield; result need not be sorted. Examples show multiplicities and various extension contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: NormalBase
rubrics_metrics.description: NormalBase(F[, elm]) (attribute) — for F a Galois extension of its LeftActingDomain, returns a list of elements forming a normal basis (a vector space basis closed under the Galois group action). If elm is given it's used as a hint for the algorithm (Artin's algorithm referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show output lists for small fields; algorithmic hint parameter can guide search for normal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFFE and related categories
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFFE / IsFFECollection / IsFFECollColl / IsFFECollCollColl (Category) — objects in IsFFE implement elements of finite fields; IsFFECollection is a collection of finite field elements of same characteristic; IsFFECollColl is a collection of such collections (e.g., matrices of finite field elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how finite field elements and their collections are classified in GAP's category system; used for dispatch of methods and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Z (for field size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Z(p^d) or Z(p,d) (function) — returns the designated generator of the multiplicative group of the finite field with p^d elements. p must be prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on representation: GAP can represent GF(p^d) under certain conditions (p^d<=65536, d=1, or known Conway polynomial). If Conway polynomial unavailable, GAP may enter break loop to attempt computation. The returned root is primitive and yields all nonzero elements as powers. Additive/multiplicative neutral elements are distinct objects from integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conway polynomial availability caution
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP can represent fields using Conway polynomials; if ConwayPolynomial(p,d) is not known and d>1, GAP may need to compute it which can be long and may trigger a break loop/error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IsCheapConwayPolynomial to check whether ConwayPolynomial will return quickly; computing Conway polynomials for composite n can be very time consuming.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLexOrderedFFE / IsLogOrderedFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: IsLexOrderedFFE(ffe) / IsLogOrderedFFE(ffe) (Category) — finite field elements can be ordered: elements in IsLexOrderedFFE are ordered lexicographically by coefficients with respect to canonical basis; elements in IsLogOrderedFFE are ordered according to discrete logarithms with respect to PrimitiveRoot attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering determines outcome of comparisons using = and < across FFEs; ordering groups elements first by characteristic then by degree. Examples illustrate comparisons and lexicographic vs logarithmic ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite field scalar operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard scalar operations apply to finite field elements: Characteristic, One, Zero, Inverse, AdditiveInverse, Order (where Order is defined for zero with value 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations are available and behave analogously to other scalar types, with noted differences in representation and special-case behavior for zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeFFE(z) / DegreeFFE(vec) / DegreeFFE(mat) (attribute/method) — returns the degree of the smallest finite field containing element z or all elements of vector/matrix over a finite field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show differing degrees for powers of primitive elements and vectors mixing elements from different extension degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: LogFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: LogFFE(z, r) (operation) — returns the discrete logarithm of element z in a finite field with respect to root r; signals error if z is zero; returns fail if z is not a power of r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrete logarithm defined as smallest nonnegative i with r^i = z; used for converting power representation to exponent.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: IntFFE(z) / Int(z) (attribute/method) — returns the integer corresponding to element z which must lie in a finite prime field; the smallest nonnegative i such that i * One(z) = z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence uses choice of Z(p) being element corresponding to smallest primitive root modulo p; installed as method for Int operation on FFEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntFFESymm
rubrics_metrics.description: IntFFESymm(z) / IntFFESymm(vec) (attribute) — for finite prime field element z, returns the integer of smallest absolute value i such that i * One(z) = z; for vectors applies entrywise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps into −p/2..p/2 range for prime field of characteristic p (p<2^16) using chosen primitive root mapping; useful for symmetric integer representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: IntVecFFE(vecffe) (operation) — returns the list of integers corresponding to vector vecffe of finite field elements in a prime field (uses IntFFE entrywise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience for converting vectors of FFEs to integer vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsInternalFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: AsInternalFFE(ffe) (operation) — return an internal FFE equal to ffe if one exists, otherwise fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to coerce external/abstract finite field elements into GAP's internal efficient representation when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: RootFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: RootFFE(F, z, k) (operation) — returns an element r in finite field F whose k-th power is z; returns fail if none exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute k-th roots in finite fields where they exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultField (for finite field elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultField(list) / DefaultRing(list) (function) — for finite field elements returns the smallest field containing the given elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate interactions when elements come from different internal representations; DefaultField chooses smallest containing field.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaloisField / GF
rubrics_metrics.description: GaloisField(p^d) / GF(p^d) and multiple forms (function) — returns a finite field. First argument specifies subfield S (prime integer or finite field), second argument specifies extension (integer d or irreducible polynomial). If integer d, uses Conway polynomial of degree d over S unless explicit polynomial provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of subfield determines over which field trace, minimal polynomial, Galois group, conjugates, norm, etc. are computed; field regarded as vector space over given subfield, determining canonical basis and dimension. Examples show BasisVectors and GaloisGroup sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimitiveRoot
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimitiveRoot(F) (attribute) — returns a primitive root of finite field F, i.e., a generator of its multiplicative group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A primitive root is always a primitive element; used for power/discrete-logarithm based representations and algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: FrobeniusAutomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: FrobeniusAutomorphism(F) (attribute) — returns the Frobenius automorphism of finite field F as a field homomorphism. Frobenius f maps each z to z^p where p is characteristic; automorphisms of F are powers of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to generate Galois group relative to prime field; i-th power maps z to p^i-th power; product of powers corresponds to addition modulo Size(F)-1; zero-th power is IdentityMapping(F). Examples show action on primitive element and raising automorphism to powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConwayPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: ConwayPolynomial(p, n) (function) — is the Conway polynomial Φ_{n,p} of GF(p^n) over the prime field GF(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: Conway polynomial is primitive, irreducible, monic, minimal polynomial of a primitive root and satisfies compatibility conditions for divisors d|n. An ordering on polynomials of degree n over GF(p) is used to choose minimal representative. GAP ships many precomputed polynomials; if not stored, GAP computes by checking polynomials in order which can be time consuming. Use IsCheapConwayPolynomial to predict runtime. RandomPrimitivePolynomial can be used when any primitive polynomial suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCheapConwayPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCheapConwayPolynomial(p, n) (function) — returns true if ConwayPolynomial(p,n) will give a result in reasonable time (either precomputed or n not too big prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to avoid invoking a potentially very long ConwayPolynomial computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomPrimitivePolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomPrimitivePolynomial(F, n[, i]) (function) — returns a primitive polynomial of degree n over finite field F (or prime power q interpreted as GF(q)). If i given, polynomial is written in variable number i. Works for much larger fields than Conway polynomials (requires factorization of |F|^n − 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative to ConwayPolynomial when any primitive polynomial suffices; relies on factoring multiplicative group order to test primitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ViewObj / PrintObj / Display for finite field elements
rubrics_metrics.description: ViewObj(z) / PrintObj(z) / Display(z) (methods) — internal finite field elements are viewed/printed/displayed as powers of the primitive root (except zero displayed as 0*primitive_root). For larger fields, elements may be printed as linear combinations of low powers of primitive root; Display uses compact 'z' notation (e.g., z2+z4+...), and ViewObj uses that compact form only if length within ViewLength; otherwise replaced by <<an element of GF(p,d)>>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show different print formats, use of primitive root notation Z(p^d)^i, representation as sums for larger fields, and special handling for very large outputs (Display prints full compact representation while ViewObj may abbreviate). Note that elements of large prime fields are displayed as residue class objects such as ZmodpZObj.

rubrics_metrics.name: CyclotomicField / CF
rubrics_metrics.description: CyclotomicField([subfield,] n) / CyclotomicField([subfield,] gens) / CF forms (function) — first form creates nth cyclotomic field Q_n, second creates smallest cyclotomic field containing elements in gens; field can be generated as extension of designated subfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CF single-argument fields are stored in global CYCLOTOMIC_FIELDS for reuse. Examples show constructing CF(5), CF with subfield arguments and generators. CF is used in context of abelian number fields.
